---
title: "Paul A. David"
description: "Economic historian of path dependence and the dynamo–computer productivity lag (1935–2023)."
toc: false
---

**Paul A. David** (1935–2023) was an economic historian at Stanford and Oxford, and the
leading theorist of *path dependence* — how small early events and increasing returns lock
technologies in (his 1985 essay "Clio and the Economics of QWERTY"). In *The Dynamo and the
Computer* (1990) he answered Solow's paradox historically: electricity took roughly forty
years to appear in the productivity statistics because factories had to be physically and
organizationally rebuilt around it. His enduring theme — general-purpose technologies pay
off only once their complements mature — is the backbone of a lot of what gets written here.
